sample_unit: kidney transplant recipient records (de-identified OPTN/UNOS cohorts)

links.outcome: Evidence attribution and predictive calibration versus baselines when outputs are grounded in retrieved authoritative sources
links.effect: KT-LLM, with retrieval-augmented grounding in Banff, OPTN and SRTR documents, outperformed strong baselines in evidence attribution and predictive calibration; no numbers reported in the abstract.
links.quote: On de-identified OPTN and UNOS cohorts, KT-LLM outperformed strong baselines in evidence attribution and predictive calibration.

unlisted_practices: Encoding regulatory and reporting timelines (OPTN/UNOS/SRTR) into executable pass/warn/fail compliance rules with versioned evidence
Versioned-source citation anchoring for auditable outputs
Subgroup clustering to surface heterogeneity within Black recipients

screen.reason: The paper introduces a new multi-agent, retrieval-augmented framework (KT-LLM) for kidney transplant modeling and evaluates its model performance and calibration retrospectively on de-identified OPTN/UNOS datasets.
